name: Christianity
summary: Christianity is the religion of the historic community deriving from Jesus of Nazareth, with the Christian Bible (Old and New Testament) as its scripture. Its stated positions on politics are few and mostly come from scripture: authority is ordained by God, the faithful pay taxes and obey rulers, wealth and possessions carry duties and dangers, Christ is the only way of salvation, and marriage and sexual conduct follow creation. Churches and traditions differ widely on most political questions, so the profile is thin.
scope: The religion as the defining reference works describe it (Britannica, the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry, World History Encyclopedia, the Catholic Encyclopedia entry), answered from the Christian Bible, which they name as its sacred texts. Denominations (Catholicism, Protestantism, Orthodoxy), Christian parties and movements, and Christian-derived ideologies are other subjects and are not used. Where scripture takes no position, or churches differ and the scripture is silent, the answer is null.

notes: Themes searched: authority and obedience, tax, wealth and poverty, marriage and sex, war and violence, animals, religion and truth. Answers rest on the Christian Bible as the defining sources name it; the New Testament was preferred where the Old and New differ. Statements on which churches differ and scripture is silent, or where the record of Christian states runs against the text (revolution, religious war, restricting conversion, equality before the law), are left null. The reference works are saved copies of their pages; Britannica's saved copy is mostly its table of contents. Wikipedia was used only to find leads. Only a handful of positions are stated, so the uncertainty rule is expected to fail.
